claims.text: The tribo-corrosion degradation of equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is governed by competition between mechanical passive-film removal and film repassivation.
Mechanical sliding intermittently strips the protective oxide/hydroxide film and exposes the underlying alloy to corrosion.
CoCrFeMnNi undergoes rapid, localized, element-specific repassivation after wear-induced exposure.
The rapid repassivation results from the compositional complexity of the HEA.
Rapid repassivation mitigates localized corrosion during sliding.
The coupled degradation is nonlinearly sub-additive relative to the sum of independently measured wear and corrosion losses.
The initial material is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial alloy has a uniform native passive film formed under ambient conditions.
Time-resolved EIS can track changes associated with passive-film resistance and integrity.
Cyclic sliding in 3.5 wt% NaCl, with static-corrosion and inert-medium wear-only controls, is proposed to isolate the coupled response.
The governing behavior is determined by the relative rates of passive-film removal and regeneration.
When repassivation is faster than film removal, total degradation is lower than the additive sum of wear-only and static-corrosion losses.
Under the proposed tribo-corrosion conditions, the wear component may remain similar to the independently measured wear component.
Under the proposed tribo-corrosion conditions, the corrosion component will be significantly reduced by rapid repassivation.
Increasing normal load beyond a critical threshold will make film removal dominate repassivation and markedly increase total degradation.
The proposed sub-additive behavior should hold for CoCrFeMnNi in 3.5 wt% NaCl at room temperature under moderate loading because this environment supports rapid repassivation.
Different electrolytes, lower temperatures, or significant compositional changes may slow repassivation and invalidate the prediction.
High mechanical loading can fracture oxide layers and increase wear in CoCrFeMnNi.
A strictly additive total loss with no film-reformation signal correlated with reduced localized corrosion would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
